result: Conservative for all camera directions under the source atlas contract; default native cache bytes unchanged.
premises: Range atlas and interval atlas belong to the same bake and resolution; tile orientation and shader V agree.
Interval sampling is bilinear at level zero with the native half-texel clamp; range atlas uses the native 8x8 plus one-texel halo summary.
Morph field retains the hard bound Fm >= F0-limit with 0 <= limit <= band; physical box sizes are positive.
Expanded cache remains separate from native distanceMap and is regenerated if source bytes, resolution, box size, or maximum band changes.
proof_steps: Fm(p)<=0 implies F0(p)<=band. F0=max_i(size_i*(max(outer_i,gap_i)-epsilon)), so every outer_i <= epsilon+band/size_i. Gaps can only remove occupancy, and need not be represented in the coarse cache.

For p in an 8-texel transverse cell, linear texture interpolation reads indices from 8*c-1 through 8*c+8. The native range baker covers exactly that 10-texel footprint in each transverse coordinate and clamps the outer atlas edge consistently.

A convex bilinear combination has high <= max(sampled high), low >= min(sampled low). Therefore the summarized range intersects the axis cell expanded by epsilon+band/size_i whenever a morphed point in that cell exists.

The implementation retains the native extra filtering texel: margins=2.5/R+band/size_i. New-cache range extrema additionally round outward by one half-float step, f32 cell bounds round outward, and a tiny f32 conversion guard is added. These only add occupied cells.
The unchanged six neighbour-min passes produce D=min(7,ChebyshevDistanceToOccupied). All cells in the centered block of radius D-1 are empty, including when D is capped at 7.

The shader preserves the fine sampling lattice: it jumps to floor((blockExit-tNear)/fineStep), then re-evaluates. This never skips a fine sample after the empty-block exit. previous remains a known-empty lattice sample for bisection.

limits: The cache proves skipped space is empty for this bounded field; it does not prove the field is Euclidean SDF.
Fine-only sampling can still miss geometry smaller than its sampling support. The cache path preserves that lattice rather than adding another stepping approximation.
